dial.summary: Real yields eased to 2.87% and DXY held flat at 102.23 while the 10Y yield maintained its retreat from the 5.35% cycle high; BTC.D firmed to 59.3% and BTC perpetual funding collapsed to 0.0031%, reinforcing deepening spot-driven accumulation ahead of October 14 CPI as the primary macro regime-shift catalyst.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.6T per StreetStats Oct 8 data ($103,649B), unchanged from prior run; 4-week trend flat — no confirmed September G4 data yet (6–8 week reporting lag); YoY growth positive so status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5% (released Oct 1, 2026; August 54.6%, 4-week change −0.1pp within flat threshold); New Orders 55.3%, Prices Paid 77.9% (highest since mid-2021); status neutral — above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis; next release November 2, 2026 for October data.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot closed at 102.23 on October 9, 2026 (Trading Economics, Rock & Turner Friday recap; Oct 8 close 102.22); 4-week trend up from ~99.9 on Sep 9 (+~2.3%); status headwind (above 100 threshold); 10Y yield retreat from 5.35% peak may provide modest DXY ceiling — sustained close below 100 required for neutral status; October 14 CPI is the next major repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 at 2.87% as of October 8, 2026 (eased 5bps from Oct 7's 2.92% cycle high; StreetStats confirms 2.87%); 4-week trend up from ~2.52% on Sep 8 (+~35bps); status headwind (rising on 4-week basis and above 2% threshold); October 14 CPI is the key repricing catalyst — a miss below 3.0% YoY could drive real yields back toward 2.5%.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 9, 2026: 10Y at 5.24%, 2Y at 4.80% → spread = +44bps (2Y rose 3bps on the day, narrowing spread from Oct 8's +47bps); 4-week trend up (steepening from ~+42bps on Sep 9 to +44bps); status supportive (positive and steepening on 4-week basis — both criteria met); FOMC Oct 27–28 and Oct 14 CPI are the next major curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6,747,560M ($6.748T) for week ending October 7, 2026 (H.4.1, released Oct 8; unchanged from prior run — Oct 10 is Saturday, next release Oct 15); 4-week trend flat: Sep 9 ~$6,737M → Oct 7 $6,748M = +$11B (+0.16%); status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau, no QT acceleration).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Binance BTCUSDT perpetual funding at 0.0031% per 8h (3.44% annualized) as of October 9, 2026 (BTC at ~$83,250); sharply declined from MacroMicro's Sep 30 cross-exchange average of 0.0067%; 4-week trend down from ~0.004–0.005% range in mid-September; status supportive (0.0031% well below 0.04% overheating threshold — confirms deepening spot-driven accumulation, not leveraged speculation).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B (DefiLlama trend data) against total crypto ~$2.87T gives ~10.7% dominance; BTC.D firmed to 59.3% (tv-hub.org, Oct 2026); 30-day trend flat: ~10.4–10.6% (Sep 9) → ~10.7% (Oct 9) = marginal rise within flat threshold; status neutral (not clearly falling on 30-day basis; headwind condition not confirmed as total market cap roughly flat).

upcoming.title: CPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the dominant macro catalyst before the October 27–28 FOMC decision; August CPI YoY was +3.4–3.5%; ISM Manufacturing Prices at 77.9% (highest since mid-2021) is a leading upside signal; a hot print above +3.5% YoY could revive October hike odds, push DXY above 104, and reverse the recent 10Y yield retreat; a dovish miss below +3.0% YoY would cement Fed hold expectations, catalyze DXY below 100, and potentially trigger a BTC breakout; real yields at 2.87% and DXY at 102.23 make this the single most important data point of the month.

upcoming.title: PPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation released the day after CPI; August PPI Final Demand was +2.8% YoY; ISM Manufacturing Prices at 77.9% is a leading signal for potential PPI upside; a hot PPI following a hot CPI would reinforce October hike expectations and likely drive DXY back above 103; released alongside Retail Sales and Initial Jobless Claims, making October 15 the most data-dense morning before the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Retail Sales for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside September PPI and Initial Jobless Claims; given the September NFP shock (+29K), a weak retail sales print would confirm broad economic softening and reinforce Fed hold narrative; a strong print alongside weak labor extends the late-cycle bifurcation signal (resilient consumer, softening employment); provides key pre-FOMC context on Q3 consumer demand ahead of the October 29 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 11, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 11, 2026 — first claims read post-Columbus Day; released alongside PPI and Retail Sales, making October 15 the most data-dense pre-FOMC morning; claims trajectory directly informs market odds for a Fed pause vs. hike at the October 27–28 meeting; a print above 200K would reinforce labor market softening following the September NFP shock of +29K.

upcoming.title: Fed Balance Sheet H.4.1 (week ended October 14, 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve H.4.1 weekly balance sheet release at 4:30 PM ET — covers week ending October 14, 2026; prior reading $6,747,560M ($6.748T, week ending Oct 7); four consecutive weeks of flat-to-marginal expansion; a shift toward contraction combined with rising overnight rates would flip status from supportive to headwind; flat or marginally expanding expected given recent stabilization trend.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production & Capacity Utilization (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board releases September 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 9:15 AM ET; completes the Q3 output picture ahead of GDP advance estimate (October 29); September ISM Manufacturing at 54.5% and Production Index at 56.7% suggest solid output growth; a miss alongside the September NFP shock would reinforce stagflation narrative (hot prices, softening activity) into the October 27–28 FOMC.
